review.summary: Fix for an incorrect parity check in the Eulerian trail sanity logic: the code checked for exactly two even-degree vertices instead of exactly two odd-degree vertices. This is a clear logic bug in production code.
review.evidence: Issue #397 explicitly states the defect: 'the existing code checks for exactly two even degree vertices' when it should check for 'exactly two odd degree vertices.' The issue also explains why the existing test didn't catch it (the test graph happened to have two even and two odd degree vertices). The fix is in src/traversals/eulerian.jl with corresponding test updates in test/traversals/eulerian.jl.
review.missing_evidence: The actual diff content is not provided, so I cannot directly inspect the code change. However, the issue description is very clear and specific about the nature of the bug and the fix.
review.validation_risks: Minimal risk. The fix is a simple logical inversion of a condition. The main risk is ensuring the test cases adequately cover edge cases (e.g., graphs with no Eulerian trail, graphs with Eulerian circuits vs trails).
suggested_tests: Test graph with all even-degree vertices (should have Eulerian circuit, not just trail)
Test graph with exactly two odd-degree vertices (should have Eulerian trail)
Test graph with more than two odd-degree vertices (should have no Eulerian trail)
Test on a graph where the old check would incorrectly pass (e.g., a graph with many vertices where only two have even degree)
